content.title: About
content.content: Gluten‑free roll is a soft bread made from gluten‑free flours (such as rice, corn or buckwheat), water, yeast and a pinch of salt. It is suitable for people with celiac disease and anyone following a gluten‑free diet. The roll has a mild flavor, light texture and can be used as a base for sandwiches, snacks or side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free rolls have surged in popularity in recent years as more consumers avoid gluten.
Xanthan gum or guar gum is often added to improve dough structure.
Rolls can be made sweet or savory depending on the filling.
Traditional Italian panini are sometimes replaced with gluten‑free rolls in diet‑focused restaurants.
In Japan, gluten‑free rolls are frequently served with tamari (wheat‑free soy sauce).

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Gluten‑free flours are easier to digest for those sensitive to gluten, reducing the risk of intestinal irritation.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many conventional baked goods, gluten‑free rolls typically contain less saturated fat.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Whole‑grain gluten‑free flours provide slow‑releasing carbohydrates that help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Gluten‑free mixes are often fortified with thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Fits many diets
items.content: Gluten‑free rolls can be incorporated into vegetarian, vegan and low‑carb diets when appropriate ingredients are used.

items.title: Allergy to other ingredients
items.content: Although gluten‑free, the product may contain nuts, soy or dairy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: To improve texture, manufacturers sometimes use additives (xanthan, guar) that may cause discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Some gluten‑free flours (e.g., rice flour) have less fiber than whole‑grain wheat alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gluten‑free roll can be eaten fresh, toasted, used as a sandwich base, wrapped with fillings, or served alongside soups and salads. It slices easily and stores well in the refrigerator.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the roll in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Warm in the oven or toaster before serving to restore softness.
